title: Targeted brain stimulation to enhance recovery after shockwave-induced blast TBI: Identifying neural biomarkers to guide treatment
text:
Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is especially common in combat Veterans and results in high costs, disability, and
significant personal impact. Blast brain injuries can impose complications that significantly affect quality of life,
such as impulsivity and dysregulated fear, which are difficult to treat with current therapies. Brain stimulation is
used to treat numerous neuropsychiatric conditions, and preliminary data suggest that this intervention may
improve recovery from brain injury. However, before this promising treatment can be used in Veterans with
blast brain injury, it will be necessary to understand how brain biomarkers can be used to optimize treatment
and identify potential candidates for stimulation. Using a pre-clinical (rodent) model of blast TBI, the current
study will define brain-based biomarkers related to increased fear and impulsivity and determine whether brain
stimulation improves these outcomes. Our ultimate goal is to use the results of our studies to inform the use of
brain stimulation to improve outcomes for Veterans living with blast TBI.

title: A Study Implementing Models for Mechanical Circulatory Support Presurgical Assessment in Congenital Heart Disease Treatment (IMMPACT)
text:
Congenital heart disease (CHD) remains the most common type of major congenital malformation and
the leading cause of mortality from birth defects with up to one third of patients with complex disease
developing heart failure (HF) in the second and third decade of life, despite an intervention. Ventricular
assist devices (VAD) in patients with CHD and HF remain underutilized, in part due to the highly variable
cardiac anatomy and complex physiology. This study will assess if a 3D printed cardiac model improves
visualization of VAD and cannula placement sites in CHD-HF patients as compared to 2D imaging
alone and if perioperative factors and patient outcomes improve in CHD-HF patients with use of 3D
printed model versus traditional imaging in VAD placement planning.

title: AI-guided CRISPR-based TB drug-resistance test with optimized crRNAs and engineered Cas enzymes
text:
Drug-resistant tuberculosis is a serious public health threat that demands faster and more accurate diagnostic
tests. This research will develop an AI-guided CRISPR-based diagnostics tool using optimized crRNA and
engineered Cas13 enzymes. By enabling early and precise detection of resistance, the project will help
improve patient outcomes and prevent the spread of hard-to-treat TB and other infectious diseases.

title: 24th Annual Rocky Mountain Virology Association Conference
text:
The twenty fourth annual meeting of the Rocky Mountain Virology Association will continue scientific
collaboration among virologists and prion biologists. Dedicated scientists from regional and national institutions,
including universities and federal laboratories, with diverse expertise and a common interest in virology meet to
promote multidisciplinary approaches, productive collaborations, and scientific inspiration. Their primary
concern is the protection of people from infectious diseases.

title: Regulating FoxA-Mediated Transcription during Liver Development
text:
The goal of this proposal is to investigate mechanisms of FoxA1 and 2 regulation necessary for the
specification of hepatic fate in the human embryo. FoxA1 and 2 dysfunction in hepatic disorders and
malignancy likely stems from subversion of these very same mechanisms. The proposed work will reveal
novel pathways for FoxA1 and 2 control, enabling future manipulation of hepatocyte differentiation and function
for study of and potential targeted intervention in liver disease and cancer.

title: Breakthrough Molecular Dynamics Research via an Anton 3 Supercomputer
text:
The Anton 3 supercomputer and data resource to be deployed at the Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center,
through this award and in partnership with D. E. Shaw Research, will enable researchers to simulate larger and
more complex biomolecular systems hundreds of times faster than any other resource available to the
biomedical community and will make the resulting simulation data readily available to all. This powerful and
unique resource will bring unprecedented understanding of fundamental processes of biology, leading to better
ways to treat disease and improve quality of life.

title: A proteomics research specialist in developing targeted mass spectrometry methods for quantifying proteins important in cancer
text:
In order to impact patients through personalized medicine, we need better technologies for measuring proteins
in clinical research. The development of targeted mass spectrometry methods will provide tools to meet this
need, ushering in new information for studying disease mechanisms, diagnosing disease, and predicting
response to therapy.

title: Somatic and germline gene transduction in mosquitoes
text:
SOMATIC AND GERMLINE GENE TRANSDUCTION IN MOSQUITOES
Narrative
Mosquitoes transmit pathogens responsible for devastating diseases such as malaria, dengue, and Zika,
impacting over 40% of the global population. Baculoviruses constitute a family of large, insect-specific DNA
viruses; we identified a baculovirus that can infect mosquitoes in a compartment-specific manner in all major
mosquito genera. We will engineer baculovirus into a tool for basic and applied genetic manipulation of
mosquitoes to develop an open-source platform for gene transduction and transgenesis that can be used by the
entire community for both basic research and applied control of vector-borne diseases.

title: Molecular and cellular mechanisms of fluid balance in C. elegans
text:
Osmolarity homeostasis is vital for human health, and robust mechanisms (e.g., thirst) have been evolved to
keep body fluid osmolarity within a narrow physiological range. However, the molecular and cellular mechanisms
underlying osmolarity sensation and regulation are surprisingly incomplete, which greatly hinders our
understanding of body fluid balance and thirst. The proposed work aims to fill these knowledge gaps by
identifying novel osmosensors and mapping neural circuits of water consumption.

title: Extreme cell growth in support of stem cell proliferation and niche exit
text:
Stem cells are special cells that replicate many times over to give rise to all the tissues of the
body in an embryo, replenish the tissues of the body over the life of an organism, and make the
sperm and egg cells that go on to make the next generation. I study the relationship between
stem cells and their supportive niche cells in a microscopic worm called C. elegans, which has
many of the same cellular features as humans. I propose to follow up on my recent discovery
that the niche and associated cells grow dramatically to support the stem cells, encourage their
proliferation, and help them make sperm and eggs.

title: Computer Aided Diagnostic System for Prostate Cancer Detection Using Quantitative Multiparametric MRI
text:
Successful completion of this proposal will result in the realization of a computer aided detection (CAD) system
for detecting and assessing the aggressiveness of prostate cancer through the use of novel user-independent
evaluation of quantitative multiparametric MRI. The system will consist of a novel quantitative prostate
phantom and software pipelines. These developments overcome the major roadblocks limiting the clinical
translation of quantitative imaging methods by developing 1) a comprehensive set of tools to validate the
quantitative parameters of interest and 2) novel CAD systems with the potential to significantly impact the
management of the disease by improving biopsy targeting in the short term and providing critical information to
confidently manage men on active surveillance in the long term.

title: An automatic deep learning platform for kidney transmission electron microscopy image analysis
text:
Although transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images serve as the gold standard in kidney disease diagnosis
and research, manual measurement is labor-intensive and introduces inter-operator variation and bias. This
project aims to develop and implement the first deep learning-based platform to automate the quantification of
morphologic features in TEM images, providing practical applications for both kidney disease research and
clinical settings. By leveraging our collective expertise in cutting-edge deep learning, electron microscopy,
ultrastructural pathology, image processing, and web-based interface development, this project aims to expedite
novel drug development for kidney disease and enhance clinical diagnosis.

title: Probing mechanistic links between endothelial aging and dementia
text:
Endothelial cells line the inner surface of blood vessels, become with dysfunctional with aging, and contribute
to age-associated vascular diseases including cognitive impairment and dementia. Study of how endothelial
cell aging contributes to dementia is limited by the lack of available models to understand cellular mechanisms
of aging and test interventions. In this application, we propose to develop a new model of endothelial cell aging
using human cells and computational approaches to identify important biological processes that contribute to
cognitive impairment and dementia.

title: Neural computations underlying flexible control of behavioral strategies and problem-solving
text:
Cognitive flexibility—the ability to adjust plans, shift strategies, or generate novel solutions in response to
changing demands—is essential for adaptive behavior and is often impaired in neuropsychiatric disorders such
as autism spectrum disorder and schizophrenia. This project will investigate the causal neural mechanisms
underlying strategy switching and problem-solving, using an integrative approach that combines computational
modeling, large-scale neural recordings, and closed-loop optogenetics to interrogate the prefrontal–hippocampal
network dynamics. The findings will reveal algorithmic and implementational principles of cognitive flexibility, and
identify circuit-level mechanisms that may inform targeted interventions for disorders involving executive
dysfunction.

title: Integrative Predictors of Temporomandibular Degenerative Joint Disease
text:
Our initiative sets a new standard in the management of Temporomandibular Degenerative Joint Disease (TM DJD)
across all ages, with a special emphasis on early diagnosis in children—a critical step for preventing long-term
musculoskeletal complications. By integrating state-of-the-art multimodal imaging, precise artificial intelligence (AI),
mobile app tracking, and real-world data, we aim to revolutionize clinical decision-making for both pediatric and adult
patients. This comprehensive approach ensures the rigorous validation and widespread dissemination of our AI models,
translating these technological advances into improved care tailored to the specific needs of every TM DJD patient, thereby
enhancing outcomes across the entire spectrum of the disease.

title: MAFA and MAFB contribute to human pancreatic beta cell maturation and function by maintaining histone methylation
text:
Type 2 diabetes (T2D) is caused by the inability to regulate blood glucose levels due to decreased islet β cell
function or mass which can been attributed to loss of β cell identity or de-differentiation. While the etiology of β
cell immaturity in T2D is unclear, impairments in transcription factor expression occur. These studies will
investigate how the transcription factors MAFA and MAFB control human β cell maturity through histone
modifications that regulate gene expression allowing for proper maturation and insulin secretion.

title: Epigenetic regulation of transcriptional programming
text:
The genomes of multicellular organisms are utilized distinctly over time and space as cells multiply and
specialize during normal development. Understanding this process is of critical biomedical significance,
as mis-regulation of the human genome underlies many diseases, including the devastating ability of
cancer cells to acquire drug resistance and to metastasize. Identifying the initial steps that poise
developmental genes for activation or repression, providing a mechanistic understanding for how regulatory
decisions occur, and discovering how cells aberrantly switch state in cancer are all critical goals of our
research.

title: Integrating cancer genomics and spatial architecture of tumor infiltrating lymphocytes
text:
Cancer patients have immune cells that potentially can attack the tumor. Knowing if these immune cells are
present around the tumor provides a way of predicting the patient’s prognosis – however, there are no
standardized ways of determining this information from patient’s biopsies. Our project addresses this challenge
through a new computational method that analyzes microscopic images of a patient’s cancer and characterize
immune cells in much higher resolution compared to what is done by pathologists.

title: Structure-guided design of SOSIP GT-trimers for bNAb induction
text: Project 2 Abstract Project 2 will generate structural information on trimers and trimer-antibody complexes to validate and improve the design of new generations of germline-targeting (GT) SOSIP trimers with Project 1 and Core B. The data will be shared with Project 1 to improve the stability, antigenicity and immunogenicity of new GT SOSIP trimer designs. Dr. Ian A. Wilson will be Project Leader and Dr. Andrew B. Ward co-Leader. Specific Aim 1. Structural determinants of GT1.1 -primed CD4 binding site responses to shaping and polishing immunogens. The GT1.1 immunogen successfully primed CD4bs responses in NHPs and gl VH1-2 knock-in mice. The C101 human clinical trial demonstrated effective priming of CD4bs responses in ~70% of participants, including sequence and structure validated VH1-2 VRC01 class and non-VRC01 class precursors. Several antibodies bind to more mature trimers, including heterologous and N276 SOSIPs despite not being part of the vaccine regimen. Here, we will use structure (x-ray crystallography, electron microscopy) and biophysical analyses to characterize primed monoclonal and polyclonal antibody responses in mice, NHPs, and humans to provide critical insights for the design of shaping and polishing immunogens. Specific Aim 2. Structure-guided improvement of apex responses to GT1.1 immunogens. GT1.1 was also designed to prime precursors of germline bNAbs to the Env apex. However, unlike CD4bs responses, apex priming is not as consistent. Hence, we will use our suite of analytical tools (structure, BCR repertoire analysis, SPR, AI predictions) to analyze monoclonal and polyclonal antibody reactivity to the apex region of the original GT1.1 immunogen. We will: (i) characterize the immune response in GT1.1-immunized humans using EMPEM to establish baseline reactivity and primed responses to GT1.1; (ii) determine high-resolution structures of inferred germline precursors and isolated MAbs by x-ray crystallography, polyclonal Abs by cryoEMPEM, and MAbs with GT1.1 immunogens by cryoEM and x-ray crystallography, to investigate the molecular basis for gl- antibody precursor recognition. These data will guide design of more effective priming trimer immunogens for the apex bNAb epitope, and then design of V2-apex shaping and polishing immunogens. Specific Aim 3. Structural characterization of epitope combination immunogens. The GT1.1 success provides a foundation for next-generation constructs to target CD4bs- and V2-apex directed bNAb precursor B cells then to prime a third epitope cluster that includes fusion peptide and V3-N332. Alternative trimer scaffolds (e.g., TTT and AI-generated designs) will facilitate these designs. EMPEM will quantify the magnitude of responses to the combined epitope immunogens to inform on optimal immunogen presentations and reduce off- target responses. We will likewise use our suite of structure and biophysical tools to validate and characterize new designs and assess their engagement with bNAb precursors, as in the above Aims. The end goal will be to evaluate and down-select candidate immunogens to identify those most appropriate for human clinical trials.

title: Targeting Senescence Specific Mechanisms of NF-κB Activation to Reverse Chronic Pulmonary Fibrosis
text:
The current study seeks to investigate the mechanisms whereby a specific type of lung cell associated with
idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) accumulates and drives the pathology of this disease. To accomplish this,
we have developed a new compound that selectively blocks the activation of a pathway that maintains these
cells in the lung. Using cell-culture, and rodent models of IPF we will further test this pathway and assess how
well this new compound could potentially treat IPF.
